message.content: Both probes from last turn now have results. That directly contradicts both c1 and c2 — the kernel's full pipeline (including FP32 rounding and truncation) stays ~4x under the contract tolerance across the entire legal domain.

message.reasoning_content:
t11 kernel sweep: max rel err 2.26e-7, zero over — c2 rebutted by kernel result (actual kernel error far below tolerance). c1's t10 pure polynomial result is odd: max_rel_err 1023 at x=-10 — that's because my probe computed integer=floor(x+0.5) but the polynomial in the kernel is for 2^fraction and I compared p (≈1) against 2^x without multiplying by 2^integer. So the probe is buggy, not the kernel. The actual kernel (t11) shows the full pipeline max error 2.26e-7 across exhaustive domain — decisive for c1 as well: the polynomial's worst error with proper scaling is ~2e-7, well under 1e-6. So c1 rebutted by t11 too (coefficients are apparently minimax-fitted; max rel err 2.26e-7). Actually t11 directly contradicts c1's statement that error exceeds 1e-6 near half-integers; exhaustive sweep covers all.

Finalize both with rebutted, citing t11. Also note t10 is inconclusive/buggy for c1 but t11 supersedes.
